subject: Commit buckets, per-token thresholds and launch surge policy
messages:
From: Samir Patil <samir@launchly.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Commit buckets, per-token thresholds and launch surge policy

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profiles and prefix-caching notes. We have a product launch in June and procurement asked me to get a firm proposal for a monthly commit structure plus how Redwood handles the expected launch-week spikes. High level:

- Traffic forecast attached (high-level): peak week expected to be ~4-5x baseline for 3 days, then tails off.
- We want a predictable per-month committed spend but need a clear surge policy for short-lived spikes without huge overage surprises.
- Can you outline committed-token buckets (monthly) with step-up windows, overage rates, and a true-up cadence? We prefer monthly true-ups but procurement sometimes asks for quarterly options.

Attached: Launchly-traffic-forecast.csv (sample forecast)

Also: are there caps you can provide on burst overages or a way to pre-purchase short-term surge capacity? What discounts do you offer across commit tiers (monthly committed tokens)?

Appreciate a workbook or example schedule we can take to procurement.

Best,
Samir
Samir Patil
Head of Infrastructure
Launchly, Inc.
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patil <samir@launchly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commit buckets, per-token thresholds and launch surge policy

Hi Samir — thanks for the forecast. This is exactly the kind of launch we design for. High level proposal below; workbook attached with token math and price ladders.

Proposal summary (monthly commits + controlled surge):
- Baseline monthly commit buckets: 500M / 1.5B / 3B tokens (three tiers we commonly use). Discount steps at each threshold: 5% / 12% / 20% off list per-token.
- Step-up (ramp) schedule: we suggest a 90-day step-up window. For a June launch we’d do: Month 1 = 50% baseline commit, Month 2 = 100% baseline, Month 3 = 150% (to cover early adoption). Workbook shows exact token counts for your forecast.
- Launch-week surge buffer: we can pre-allocate a short-term surge bucket (one-week burst capacity) priced at a blended cap rate (e.g., 1.5x committed rate) and an absolute daily max to prevent runaway spend. If you prefer, we can instead hold a $X credit to be consumed only during the surge window.
- True-up cadence: monthly true-up by default (preferred for visibility). Quarterly true-up is available but requires a larger initial reserve and will affect discount negotiation.
- Overage and caps: overage beyond surge buffer billed at overage rate with a monthly cap set as a percent of committed tokens (we propose 40% for launch months).

Next steps: 1) I attached a workbook (Redwood-commit-buckets-workbook.xlsx) that maps your CSV forecast to concrete commit numbers and dollars, 2) Let us know whether you want monthly or quarterly true-ups, 3) If procurement wants firm contract language we can share a term sheet + example DocuSign.

Attachments: Redwood-commit-buckets-workbook.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks — looping Marissa to advise on pricing concessions and Monica on account coordination.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: Launchly negotiation levers and proposed concession matrix

Marissa/Monica — quick internal note so we have alignment before we go back to procurement. Key negotiation levers for this deal:

- Ramp shape: push for 90-day step-up (reduces initial concession) instead of immediate full commit.
- Surge buffer: charge a pre-purchased one-week surge bucket at 1.5x committed rate rather than open overage; that gives them predictability.
- True-up cadence: default monthly — only allow quarterly if they accept a higher minimum commit in months 1–3. Procurement will push quarterly to simplify their ops, but commercial prefers monthly for cashflow.
- Discount concession matrix (suggested):
  - 500M/mo -> 5% discount (list price baseline)
  - 1.5B/mo -> 12% discount
  - 3B+/mo -> 20% discount + optional dedicated capacity add-on pricing

If procurement asks for a guaranteed ramp (e.g., Month1 25% Month2 50% Month3 100%), we can offer a one-time launch-credit of up to $12k to offset initial overages in exchange for committing to the 6-month cadence.

Please review the workbook I sent to Samir and flag any pricing floors we shouldn’t go below on concessions. I want to be able to present a clean term sheet next week.

-Aditya
From: Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@launchly.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patil <samir@launchly.com>, Gina Torres <procurement@launchly.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commit buckets, per-token thresholds and launch surge policy

Thanks Aditya — the workbook is helpful. A couple of small asks from procurement before we proceed to terms:

On Thu, Mar 22, 2026 at 11:05 AM Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com> wrote:
> Proposal summary (monthly commits + controlled surge):
> - Baseline monthly commit buckets: 500M / 1.5B / 3B tokens (three tiers we commonly use).
> - Step-up (ramp) schedule: we suggest a 90-day step-up window.
> - Launch-week surge buffer: pre-allocate a short-term surge bucket priced at a blended cap rate (e.g., 1.5x committed rate) and an absolute daily max.
> - True-up cadence: monthly true-up by default.

Procurement questions:
1) Can you confirm that the surge buffer is transferable across months if unused? We prefer flexible credits if possible.
2) Procurement would like the option of a quarterly true-up instead of monthly — can Redwood provide a halfway option: monthly reporting with quarterly financial true-up?
3) Please confirm the DocuSign workflow and who will be the signee for Redwood.

We attached our standard procurement terms for legal review (Launchly-procurement-terms.docx). If those are fine, can you send a redlined term sheet and the DocuSign link so we can get approvals?

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Zhou
Director, Product Operations
Launchly, Inc.
